newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise fuelled by mortgage credit paper.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise fuelled by mortgage credit paper.

text.p: Danish bond prices were pushed up by rising mortgage credit paper on Friday with further gains not ruled out next week.
"It is the ongoing demand for mortgage bonds which is rubbing off positively on the whole market, the situation will probably continue after the weekend," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.10 point from the opening at 104.41, yielding 7.33 percent in turnover of 830 million crowns while its September future fell 0.80 point to 104.28 with one contract traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.40 point to 82.50.
The crown traded at 3.8662 per mark at 1030 gmt, up very marginally from around 3.8665 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 95 during the course of the morning.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of 300-400 million crowns worth of the six percent 2002 bond as part of its routine financing operations.
